nodes.summary: Stand up the Python project root, environment, dependency manifest, package layout, and test runner.
nodes.instructions:
Create the project root: pyproject.toml (Python 3.11+, fastapi, uvicorn, httpx2, pytest), a
committed uv.lock, the .venv convention, tests/ with conftest.py, and the application package
`fxrates_app` (config, ecb, rates, history, convert, commands modules are added by later stories).
Document module ownership: persistence is reached only through the shipped `persistence` package;
no database driver is imported in application code. Record the module ownership table and the
technology stack in ARCHITECTURE.md.
nodes.name: Stand up the Python project root, environment, dependency manifest, package layout, and test runner.

nodes.summary: Declare the rates table and every repository operation the stories need; Drydock generates the persistence package.
nodes.instructions:
Author-level contract only; the builder writes no persistence code. Declare one table `rates`
(date TEXT, currency TEXT, rate TEXT, PK surrogate id, UNIQUE (date, currency)). Declare an
operation for each need: upsert a rate by (date, currency); list all rates for a date; the latest
publication date on or before a date; the latest publication date overall; count of dates and
rates; first and last date; distinct currencies ascending; history list for a currency between
optional bounds ordered by date ascending; and a reset operation that removes every row for init.
nodes.name: Declare the rates table and every repository operation the stories need; Drydock generates the persistence package.

nodes.summary: Provide the cli package entry point, the dispatcher, and the executable `fxrates` at the application root.
nodes.instructions:
Implement `cli.main(argv) -> int`, `cli/testing.py` with `cli_runner`, and the executable
`fxrates` (POSIX sh launcher activating .venv, executable bit set) that exits with main's code.
The dispatcher maps a command name to a handler registered by the command stories; diagnostics go
to standard error. This story proves only the interface: main returns an int and the executable runs.

nodes.summary: Report usage errors with exit 2, empty stdout, and one stderr line.
nodes.instructions:
Validate arguments before any handler runs: no command, an unknown command, a wrong argument
count (init takes 0, load takes 1, fetch takes 0, serve takes optional --port <n>), and --port
not an integer or outside 1 to 65535 all exit 2 with empty stdout and exactly one stderr line.
Validation happens before any socket or database is touched.
nodes.name: Report usage errors with exit 2, empty stdout, and one stderr line.

nodes.summary: Provide bin/test.sh running the pytest suite offline, exiting zero only when every test passes.
nodes.instructions:
Write a POSIX sh `bin/test.sh` that cd's to the application root, activates .venv, and runs
`pytest -q`, propagating its exit status. No test opens a network connection; downloads are
stubbed. The builder adds tests alongside each story's code.
nodes.name: Provide bin/test.sh running the pytest suite offline, exiting zero only when every test passes.

nodes.summary: Resolve the database location from DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db.
nodes.instructions:
Implement `fxrates_app.config.database_path()` and a shared helper that opens the store through
`persistence.open_database`. DATABASE_URL may carry an optional `sqlite://` prefix; unset or empty
falls through to DATABASE_PATH, then `data/app.db`. Application code never imports a driver.
nodes.name: Resolve the database location from DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db.

nodes.instructions:
Implement `fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history(text)` returning a list of (date, currency, rate_text)
for non-N/A values, raising `RejectedFile` otherwise. Rules: header first field `Date`, other
fields three-letter uppercase codes, the empty trailing field from the trailing comma ignored;
every row has the header's field count; dates are real calendar YYYY-MM-DD and unique within the
file; values are `N/A` or match [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? and are nonzero. The entire file is checked
before returning. Rates keep their published text.

nodes.summary: Validate a whole ECB history file before any write.
nodes.instructions:
Implement `fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history(text)` returning a list of (date, currency, rate_text)
for non-N/A values, raising `RejectedFile` otherwise. Rules: header first field `Date`, other
fields three-letter uppercase codes, the empty trailing field from the trailing comma ignored;
every row has the header's field count; dates are real calendar YYYY-MM-DD and unique within the
file; values are `N/A` or match [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? and are nonzero. The entire file is checked
before returning. Rates keep their published text.
nodes.name: Validate a whole ECB history file before any write.

nodes.summary: `fxrates load <csv>` stores published rates as text, replacing existing rows, and reports dates,rates counts.
nodes.instructions:
Register the load handler. Read the file, parse and validate fully, then upsert each rate in one
transaction so a reader sees all or none of the load. A rejected file exits 3, prints nothing to
stdout, writes one stderr line, and stores nothing. On success print `dates,rates` then
`<dates>,<rates>` where dates counts dates with at least one stored rate in the file and rates the
rates stored. A file of only N/A prints 0,0 and stores nothing. Reloading leaves data unchanged.
nodes.name: `fxrates load <csv>` stores published rates as text, replacing existing rows, and reports dates,rates counts.

nodes.summary: `fxrates load <csv>` stores published rates as text, replacing existing rows, and reports dates,rates counts.
nodes.instructions:
Register the load handler. Read the file, parse and validate fully, then upsert each rate in one
transaction so a reader sees all or none of the load. A rejected file exits 3, prints nothing to
stdout, writes one stderr line, and stores nothing. On success print `dates,rates` then
`<dates>,<rates>` where dates counts dates with at least one stored rate in the file and rates the
rates stored. A file of only N/A prints 0,0 and stores nothing. Reloading leaves data unchanged.
nodes.name: `fxrates load <csv>` stores published rates as text, replacing existing rows, and reports dates,rates counts.

nodes.summary: GET /convert computes exact, half-even rounded conversions.
nodes.instructions:
Parameters from, to, amount [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?, optional date; without date use the latest
publication. EUR has rate 1. rate = rate(to)/rate(from) rounded half-even to six decimals;
result = amount*rate(to)/rate(from) computed exactly from stored rates, rounded half-even to two
decimals; use decimal throughout. Return strings with exactly six and two decimals; amount is
echoed as given. Same from and to gives rate 1.000000. Amount 0 gives 0.00.
nodes.name: GET /convert computes exact, half-even rounded conversions.

nodes.summary: GET /convert computes exact, half-even rounded conversions.
nodes.instructions:
Parameters from, to, amount [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?, optional date; without date use the latest
publication. EUR has rate 1. rate = rate(to)/rate(from) rounded half-even to six decimals;
result = amount*rate(to)/rate(from) computed exactly from stored rates, rounded half-even to two
decimals; use decimal throughout. Return strings with exactly six and two decimals; amount is
echoed as given. Same from and to gives rate 1.000000. Amount 0 gives 0.00.
nodes.name: GET /convert computes exact, half-even rounded conversions.

nodes.summary: GET /history/{code} lists ascending points between optional bounds.
nodes.instructions:
Return currency, base EUR, and points [{date, rate text}] ascending for dates from start through
end inclusive; both optional. start later than end gives 200 with an empty result.
nodes.name: GET /history/{code} lists ascending points between optional bounds.
